Quick answers inline:

- Endpoint migration checklist: See the spreadsheet; key items are: rotate API keys, set per-route rate limits in our Console, enable prefix cache for repeated prompts, and configure a canary model route for 10% of traffic.
- Retry and idempotency: We recommend client-side idempotency keys for non-streaming write-style requests and server-side token-safe retries for generation calls. Vivek added a short code pattern below.

Tara — quick technical notes and a sample retry pattern we use in production. Will bring more details in Monday's call.

1) Recommended client config for Node.js SDK (defaults to conservative rates):
- requestTimeoutMs: 8000
- maxRetries: 3 (exponential backoff: base 300ms)
- concurrencyPerConnection: 3

2) Rate-limit handling: honor 429 with Retry-After header; if absent, back off: 500ms -> 1s -> 2s + jitter. Add circuit-breaker that trips after 10 consecutive 429s per minute and falls back to a cached response or a lighter model.

3) Idempotency key pattern (non-streaming):
const axios = require('axios');
async function callGeneration(payload) {
  const key = payload.request_id || generateUUID();
  return axios.post('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', payload, {
    headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': key, 'Authorization': 'Bearer xxxxx' },
    timeout: 8000
  });
}

4) Streaming resume: for streaming responses we include a resume token in headers when possible. If connection drops, client should reconnect and supply the last sequence token — runtime will replay missing tokens if available (subject to cache window).

5) Endpoint migration checklist highlights (from spreadsheet):
- Create dedicated API keys for migration and tag them for 30d expiry.
- Configure route-level quotas in Console to mirror current vendor limits, then gradually increase.
- Instrument latency and token-cost metrics (we provide per-token breakdown).

Attachments: small sdk snippet files included in sdk_samples_v2.zip.

—Vivek
